moments.title: Luther's New Testament
moments.body:
Luther translates the New Testament into German in 11 weeks while in hiding at the Wartburg.

He draws on East Central German chancellery usage.
moments.takeaway: A theological translation became a literary instrument for shaping a vernacular.

moments.title: Complete Luther Bible
moments.body: The complete German Bible is published, helped by movable-type printing. Its language spreads rapidly across the Protestant lands.
moments.takeaway: Religious upheaval and print technology produced lasting linguistic standardisation.

moments.title: Brothers Grimm's Marchen
moments.body:
The Grimms publish their tale collection.

Their later Deutsches Worterbuch project is begun in 1838 and only completed in 1961.
moments.takeaway: Romantic-era philology gave the German language new tools for its own study.

now.title: German today
now.body: German is the most widely spoken native language in the EU (about 95 million speakers). Spelling reform (1996, revised 2006) and gender-inclusive writing debates continue.
now.open_questions: How will written German respond to inclusive writing debates? How does Swiss German diglossia evolve in digital contexts?

items.reflection: Even after centuries of standardisation, German continues to be the focus of language reform debates.

moments.title: Critique of Pure Reason
moments.body: Kant's first critique restructures epistemology by distinguishing what can be known from how the mind structures experience.
moments.takeaway: A single book set the agenda of European philosophy for two centuries.

moments.title: What is Enlightenment?
moments.body: Kant's essay defines enlightenment as 'man's emergence from his self-imposed nonage'.
moments.takeaway: Short essays can serve as the public face of long philosophical projects.

moments.title: Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit
moments.body:
Hegel completes the Phenomenology as Napoleon's army approaches.

His dialectical method will shape Marx, theology and 20th-century philosophy.
moments.takeaway: German Idealism developed in close proximity to political upheaval.

now.title: Philosophy in German today
now.body: Frankfurt School traditions, analytic philosophy in German universities and ongoing translation projects keep German philosophy active in current debates.
now.open_questions: How are 19th-century concepts being reread for contemporary problems in technology and ethics?

items.reflection: A small Prussian university town produced philosophy that reshaped a continent's thinking.

moments.title: Klemperer's LTI
moments.body: Klemperer publishes a philological study of the language of the Third Reich, drawing on diaries kept through the war.
moments.takeaway: Linguistic documentation under dictatorship produced a study read for generations.

moments.title: Gunter Grass's Die Blechtrommel
moments.body:
The novel addresses Nazism, war and post-war silence from inside the Polish-German borderlands.

Grass's later Nobel Prize comes in 1999.
moments.takeaway: Post-war German writing wrestled with questions earlier institutions had avoided.

moments.title: Reunification
moments.body:
The Berlin Wall fell in November 1989; full political unification followed on 3 October 1990.

German literature and language absorb the East-West encounter.
moments.takeaway: A political event reshaped what 'German' meant institutionally and culturally.

now.title: German letters today
now.body: Contemporary writers (Daniel Kehlmann, Jenny Erpenbeck, Saša Stanišić) address migration, memory and Europe's recent past. Translation flows are robust.
now.open_questions: How will writing in German evolve as the country's demographics diversify?

items.reflection: Some of Germany's most influential 20th-century literature came from writers who had to leave or who returned from exile.

moments.title: First Duden dictionary
moments.body: Duden's orthographic dictionary becomes the de facto standard reference, reinforced by the Orthographic Conference of 1901.
moments.takeaway: Standardisation of writing required private and state cooperation.

moments.title: Spelling reform agreed
moments.body:
Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Luxembourg agree a spelling reform implemented in stages.

Major newspapers reverse and re-adopt aspects through the 2000s; the revised version is settled in 2006.
moments.takeaway: Coordinated language reform across multiple states is politically difficult.

moments.title: Capital eszett accepted
moments.body:
The capital ss (uppercase eszett) is officially accepted.

Gender-neutral writing remains contested.
moments.takeaway: Orthographic change continues into the 21st century.

now.title: German varieties today
now.body: Swiss German diglossia persists; Austrian German has its own standard variety. Dialect maintenance varies sharply by region.
now.open_questions: Will digital communication accelerate convergence or maintain dialect distinctness?

items.reflection: What we call 'German' is a family of related standards and dialects, not a single uniform language.
